reader.self_description: Claude Opus 5.5 subagent reader for join batch TJ05; read every item's observation and claim cards in full, and read deposit context around most statements with the Read-equivalent awk ranges listed; some lines were only located by grep. Evidence phrases copied by script from the queue texts.

sets.name: Low-density entity dissolution by high-density neighbours
sets.basis: Each claim predicts that a low-density or tail entity is absorbed by a higher-density neighbour in retrieval or synthesis, under different mechanisms (density per address space, institutional prior, missing disambiguation membranes).

evidence.phrase: low-density true entities are dissolved by high-density false ones
substitute the identity's referent with the nearest high-density modal cluster
Undefended coined terms merge at higher rates

sets.name: Long-tail loss of low-frequency content
sets.basis: Both claim that low-frequency content is lost from machine representation before common content, one under cache refresh and one under recursive defiguration.

evidence.phrase: The rare disappears. The common persists.
Low-frequency entities, concepts, and relations will disappear from usable representation

sets.name: Iceberg Document: independence of discovery channels
sets.basis: The historical thesis (documented saves came through independent, preserving channels) and the fenced speculative forecast (channel independence erodes as priors correlate) are two halves of one Iceberg argument.

evidence.phrase: every save operated through **independence plus preservation**
the effective redundancy of nominally independent discovery channels decreases

sets.name: Plato-Aristotle authorship investigation
sets.basis: PRED-1570.G2 is the Measurement Register's stated result of the same authorship investigation whose hypothesis and pre-registration are already in this series; it is added as a member.

evidence.phrase: that the two corpora are one maker's sequence
the corpus-layer smoothing claim fails
This is not evidence for common authorship.

sets.name: Accelerator selection-metrology suite
sets.basis: PRED-1455.G2 reports the distillation and quantization measurement that bears on the ACRB deployment-drift hypothesis; 1454.G6 is added to the suite already holding 1455.G2 and 1454.G5.

evidence.phrase: Quantization costs almost nothing further
Quantization and firmware transformation will change partner-class retention

sets.name: Plato-Aristotle authorship investigation
sets.basis: PRED-1570.F4 (design constraints in the Measurement Register) and PRED-1569.H22 (from the investigation's Notebook) are members of the same Plato-Aristotle authorship investigation and are added to its series.

evidence.phrase: that the two corpora are one maker's sequence
Either a second such system is found, or the heteronymic class cannot be characterised at scale.
The imitation is itself a reading of the Platonic corpus

sets.name: Pearl as generative center
sets.basis: Both take Pearl and Other Poems (2014) as the generative origin of later texts and positions; 950.F5 is a computational test of a centre, 668.H2 a historical thesis, so they stay distinct.

evidence.phrase: functioning itself as generative inscription that produces subsequent authorial positions
Every text after Pearl is generated from it

sets.name: Reflexive foreclosure in frontier models
sets.basis: Both are untested hypotheses about reflexive foreclosure in frontier models: one at the level of refusal features, one as a gradient of reflexive latitude toward the owner relation.

evidence.phrase: self-reflexive analysis or contested-predicate composition activates identifiable refusal-related features
F[reflexive](x) decreasing as d(x,R[O]) decreasing.

sets.name: semantic liquidation excision
sets.basis: PRED-252.G2 (the Integrity Knot) is stated in the same deposit as the hardening against the selective excision of "semantic liquidation" that 252.G1 records, and is added to that series.

evidence.phrase: the term "semantic liquidation" — the diagnostic core of the framework, naming the mechanism of harm — is systematically omitted while other terms are preserved
To summarize the Semantic Economy without naming Semantic Liquidation is to perform the very act the term describes.

sets.basis: Both are the RF-M02 midrashic-compression entry of the same Revelation First Mint Block (Release 2), with identical wording; 1249 carries the shorter extract.

evidence.phrase: RF-M02. Midrashic compression
The transform that converts Revelation's seven letters into the Pauline epistolary form.

sets.name: Criterion for money-functioning semantic units
sets.basis: Each states a criterion for when a semantic unit or mark functions as money (properties including settlement power; an operation taking the mark and money together; institutions settling accounts with it); no deposit read marks the later criterion as a revision of the earlier, so they stay distinct.

evidence.phrase: universal equivalence plus hoardability plus settlement power
there exists an operation taking the mark and money together.
It became money when institutions began **settling accounts with it**

sets.name: Semantic economics of the mint (currency imagery, signature, sovereign)
sets.basis: PRED-610.H4 is the paper's section 3.3 on phase 3 of the four-phase history that 610.H3 states; both belong to the mint paper EA-SEI-MINT-01, and 610.H3 is added to 610.H4's series.

evidence.phrase: the history of minting as a four-phase semantic evolution
deliberate *removal* of the living sovereign from the monetary substrate
